html:
A Japanese warrior leader who won the Genpei War and founded the Kamakura shogunate, the first government run by samurai. Some form of military rule over Japan followed from his time until 1868.

His father was killed in 1160 when the rival Taira clan won control of the court, and the boy Yoritomo was exiled to Izu in the east. There he married Hōjō Masako, daughter of a local warrior. In 1180 he rose against the Taira and gathered the warriors of eastern Japan behind him. His half-brother Yoshitsune won the war at sea at Dan-no-ura in 1185. Yoritomo then turned on Yoshitsune and hunted him to his death.

Yoritomo stayed at Kamakura, far from the court at Kyoto, and set up his own offices. He placed his men as constables and stewards across the provinces. In 1192 the emperor named him shogun.

He died in 1199 after a fall from his horse. His sons did not keep power for long; his wife's family, the Hōjō, ruled as regents. The Kamakura shogunate lasted until 1333.
